बॉलीवुड जगत से आई एक बेहद चौंकाने वाली और बुरी खबर! 🚨
मशहूर फिल्ममेकर संजय गुप्ता का 59 साल की उम्र में शनिवार सुबह अचानक निधन हो गया। 💔
मुंबई में उनके घर पर पुलिस के मुताबिक, सीसीटीवी फुटेज में देखा गया कि रात करीब 2 बजे वह ड्राइंग रूम से किचन में गए और संतुलन बिगड़ने से दीवार से जा गिरे। 🎥
वर्सोवा पुलिस ने एक्सीडेंटल डेथ रिपोर्ट दर्ज कर ली है और मामले की जांच कर रही है। 👮‍♂️
अनिल कपूर, अजय देवगन और विवेक ओबेरॉय समेत कई सितारों ने सोशल मीडिया पर और उनके घर जाकर श्रद्धांजलि दी। 🙏
क्या आपने उनकी कोई फिल्म थिएटर्स में देखी है? 🎬

ctx.title: Sanjay Gupta death: Ajay Devgn says the director had so much more cinema left in him, Anil Kapoor admits he is ‘deeply saddened and heartbroken’
ctx.summary: Sanjay Gupta died at his residence after he slipped and hit his head. He was 59.
ctx.text:
Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has died at the age of 59. His sudden death on Saturday morning has sent a shock waves through the film industry. Following his death, several actors and friends visited his home in Mumbai to pay their last respects. Many others took to social media to remember him and pay their tribute.
Anil Kapoor paid an emotional tribute on X. He worked with filmmaker Sanjay Gupta in two films: Musafir (2004) and Shootout at Wadala (2013). He wrote, "Deeply saddened and heartbroken by Sanjay's passing. We shared a special bond, both personally and through the films we worked on together. There was always an understanding between us that I truly cherished. Sanjay had his own unique voice and vision as a filmmaker, and the memories of working with him will always remain close to my heart. Going to miss you, Sanjay. Rest in peace, my friend."
Meanwhile, Ajay Devgn wrote, "Gone far too soon. Sanjay had so much more cinema left in him, so many more years and stories ahead. Truly heartbreaking….praying for strength and peace for his family."
Vivek Oberoi also recalled memories of working with Sanjay and said, "I am deeply shocked and heartbroken by the sudden and untimely demise of Sanjay Gupta. This loss is truly unimaginable and very difficult to process.
Having worked together, this news feels deeply personal. It is never easy to accept the loss of someone you have shared a journey, conversations and memories with. Some news leaves you numb, and this is one of those moments.
I will always cherish the time we spent working together. You will be missed, Sanjay. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. May God give them the strength to cope with this irreparable loss.
The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are probing to ascertain the exact sequence of events. The police were informed in the morning about the death of Sanjay Gupta.
The police said the CCTV footage of the house shows that around 2.00 am. Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen and later lost his balance and fell against the wall.
Born in 1967 in Mumbai, Sanjay Gupta began his career at age 26 with the 1994 release, Aatish: Feel the Fire, starring Sanjay Dutt, Aditya Pancholi, Raveena Tandon, Karisma Kapoor and Atul Agnihotri.
Over the next few years, he developed expertise in making gangster films, culminating in the 2002 film Kaante, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt,. Suniel Shetty, Kumar Gaurav, Lucky Ali, and Mahesh Manjrekar. Widely regarded as his best work and one of the best gangster films to come out of Bollywood, it was inspired by Quentin Tarantino's Reservoir Dogs. He followed this up with critically acclaimed and successful films such as Zinda, starring Sanjay Dutt and John Abraham. One of his most high-profile films was the Hrithik Roshan -starrer Kaabil, which earned ₹ 208 crore worldwide, emerging as his highest-grosser.
Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and film festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent film/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’.

A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified film critic. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own.
